paper_memo.memo_title: Analytical & Source-Audit Memo: CMS-7 — Military Activities in the EEZ: A U.S.-China Dialogue on Security and International Law in the Maritime Commons (Peter Dutton, ed., December 2010)

sections.heading: 1. Strategic Context & Core Thesis
sections.body: China Maritime Study No. 7 records a 2009 workshop in which American and Chinese officers, lawyers and scholars set out their positions on a question that had produced the 2001 EP-3 and 2009 Impeccable incidents: may a coastal state restrict foreign military activities such as surveys and reconnaissance in its exclusive economic zone? The Chinese authors argue that military surveys are effectively marine scientific research or are barred by coastal-state security interests; the American authors argue UNCLOS preserves traditional freedoms and limits coastal-state authority to resources and the environment. The editor concludes the friction is less about legal technicalities than about China's aim to increase control over its near seas versus U.S. freedom of navigation.

sections.heading: 2. Section-by-Section Analytical Breakdown
sections.body:
• **Introduction (Dutton)**: Workshop context; the U-shaped line; the EEZ dispute; implications.
• **Chapter 1 (Peng Guangqian)**: China's maritime rights and interests.
• **Chapter 2 (Pedrozo)**: U.S. views on marine data collection.
• **Chapter 3 (Yu Zhirong)**: Jurisprudential analysis of U.S. Navy military surveys.
• **Chapter 4 (Williams)**: Aerial reconnaissance by military aircraft.
• **Chapter 5 (Wu Jilu)**: The concept of marine scientific research.
• **Chapter 6 (Kraska)**: Resources rights and environmental protection; the functional approach.
• **Chapter 7 (Xue Guifang)**: Surveys and research activities in the EEZ.
• **Chapter 8 (Wachman)**: Playing by or playing with the rules of UNCLOS?

sections.heading: 3. Key Doctrinal Concepts, Terminology & Quantitative Claims
sections.body:
• **Concepts**: *exclusive economic zone (EEZ)*, *U-shaped / nine-dashed line*, *marine scientific research*, *military survey*, *hydrographic survey*, *due regard*, *sovereign immunity*, *innocent passage*, *creeping jurisdiction*, *functional approach*, *internationally lawful uses of the sea*.
• **Quantitative claims**: EEZ `~38%` of the world's oceans; incidents `75–80` miles southeast of Hainan; James Bank `~50 nm` off Borneo (`~4°N`); Chinese offshore interests from `200 nm` east to `1,600 nm` south; `4` schools of thought on the nine-dashed line; workshop `4` months after Impeccable; `8` chapters.

sections.heading: 4. Audit Assessment & Analytical Significance
sections.body:
Of the 6 reference rows audited in `CMS-07`, 4 are rated `ok` and 2 are rated `unk`; no `fix` was found:
• **`[CMS07-R04]` (`unk` — Military Surveys as Marine Scientific Research)**: A contested legal interpretation not shared by most maritime states.
• **`[CMS07-R06]` (`unk` — Interpretive Conclusions)**: The 'moral primacy' framing and restraint proposal are untested.

The volume is the **best two-sided statement of the U.S.–China EEZ legal dispute** and remains the reference for legal arguments alongside the 2010 incident-management study (`CMS-06`) and later dispute/survey studies (`CMS-15`, `CMR-03`). These publications are not themselves a chronology of incidents. Its limits are the 2010 date, the focus on legal positions rather than operational practice, and the abbreviated treatment of the nine-dash line, which the 2016 arbitral award later addressed.

**Footnote rows**: all 319 footnotes were extracted and consolidated into 222 source rows in the Reference Audit Matrix (CMS07-S2N001 to CMS07-S10N024). Repeat citations of the same source within this paper, including Ibid. and short-form notes, share one row, which lists each note's passage and result. Footnote-level result: 319 notes: 134 (42%) are confirmed, 1 of them against a retrieved source and 133 after an outside web search (94 of the latter with a slip or an unchecked detail noted); 9 are flagged for reader check; 185 (58%) are not confirmed. Of the 185 notes not confirmed, 12 are Chinese-language sources that have not been searched in Chinese (a search in Chinese could settle some of them); 34 were judged not web-checkable (26 print-only books or paywalled items; 6 notes that are explanatory text or a fragment, not a citation; 2 other items); 138 were searched on the web without finding corroboration; 1 has not been searched. A source row is `ok` only when every note in it is confirmed, and `fix` when a note is confirmed wrong; the paper's 222 source rows are 89 `ok`, 0 `fix` and 133 `unk`. Notes flagged for reader check, for example (the outside search found something a reader should look at; none is a finding that the author is wrong): `CMS07-S4N019`: The sentence says the State Department excludes Argo and ocean-observation programs and archaeological wreck activities from MSR; sources found say hydrographic and military activities are excluded, while a 2018 State slide lists Argo floats as 'still include in some cases' when deployed in an EEZ. The current State Department…; `CMS07-S4N030`: The sentence says that in February 1974 a Soviet reconnaissance aircraft conducting a surveillance mission off the coast of Alaska ran low on fuel and made an emergency landing at Gambell; `CMS07-S5N010`: The sentence says that on 26 April 2001 the writer led a team aboard R/V Roger Revelle, a U.S.-operated ship doing marine scientific research in China's sea areas with prior permission; and 6 more. 62 notes carry a reader note on how the note is displayed or cited.

sections.heading: Open claim-audit follow-up, November 22, 2026 (review complete; gaps recorded)
sections.body:
This continuation targets 11 initially open claim audits in this paper. 11 have a recorded individual follow-up: 1 now have a supported or correction finding; 10 remain unresolved. 0 of this paper’s initial open audits still await this continuation. Every reviewed row retains its evidence limits; a completed follow-up does not mean every substantive claim is verified.

[CMS07-R04](#audit?type=claim&paper=CMS-07&row=CMS07-R04): Reviewed; unresolved. Original passage-level comparison for the attributed argument and activity-specific evidence for any pollution allegation; the competing treaty interpretations remain distinct.

[CMS07-R06](#audit?type=claim&paper=CMS-07&row=CMS07-R06): Reviewed; unresolved. Contemporaneous negotiating records for the historical claim and the exact Ma speech for its quotation; no empirical test establishes the recommended compromise.

[CMS07-R08](#audit?type=claim&paper=CMS-07&row=CMS07-R08): Reviewed; unresolved. A daily ship log, consent instrument or independent contemporary record for April 26, 2001.

[CMS07-R13](#audit?type=claim&paper=CMS-07&row=CMS07-R13): Reviewed; unresolved. The specific pre-2009 studies and mitigation conditions underlying the assertion, with behavior, injury and species scope distinguished.

[CMS07-R19](#audit?type=claim&paper=CMS-07&row=CMS07-R19): Reviewed; unresolved. The specific national requirement, date, jurisdiction and relevant adjudication or legal analysis; the treaty text is not incident evidence.

[CMS07-R41](#audit?type=claim&paper=CMS-07&row=CMS07-R41): Supported within the documented scope. The conference documents do not establish the term’s first use anywhere; no such wider priority claim is certified.

[CMS07-R43](#audit?type=claim&paper=CMS-07&row=CMS07-R43): Reviewed; unresolved. The cited commentary and attributable drafting discussion explaining the choice, rather than inferring subjective intention from the final words.

[CMS07-R49](#audit?type=claim&paper=CMS-07&row=CMS07-R49): Reviewed; unresolved. Specific Chinese measures or incidents and the corresponding official rationale; separate phrase-count/drafting history from conduct.

[CMS07-R52](#audit?type=claim&paper=CMS-07&row=CMS07-R52): Reviewed; unresolved. An attributable drafting history for the claimed derivation and the precise cited commentary for the civil-aviation analogy.

[CMS07-R59](#audit?type=claim&paper=CMS-07&row=CMS07-R59): Reviewed; unresolved. A defined set of cases/respondents, applicable legal conditions and actual refusal records, with response bias and classifications stated.

[CMS07-R66](#audit?type=claim&paper=CMS-07&row=CMS07-R66): Reviewed; unresolved. A historical country-by-country inventory or the original survey with nonresponse limits and specified missing procedures.

rows.source: Core Chinese Position: 'The Arctic Belongs to All Humankind,' the Sovereignty Quandary (Jakobson), 'Inserting Hands' (chashou), the 'Right to Speak Up' (huayu quan), a Chinese Admiral's 20 Percent Population / 20 Percent Resources Remark (Introduction, pp. 1–8)
rows.usage: Establishes the main finding that China's Arctic policy rests on a 'common heritage' premise and a desire for influence.
rows.finding: Consistent with the cited Chinese sources (`ok`): the 'common heritage of all humankind' language and the debate over a 'right to speak up' are documented in quoted Chinese articles and in Jakobson's 2010 SIPRI study; the admiral's 20 percent remark is attributed to an unnamed 'Chinese admiral' (Note 22) and the author himself says it does not amount to official policy.

rows.source: Resource and Route Claims: Northwest Passage Shortening Routes by 5,200–7,000 Nautical Miles; 'Standard Observation' of 25 Percent of the World's Oil and Gas and 9 Percent of Its Coal; Estimates Quoted from the U.S. Geological Survey (Introduction, pp. 3, 8; Scholarly Writing, pp. 18–19)
rows.usage: Documents the economic assumptions that drive Chinese interest and rhetoric.
rows.finding:
**Open-claim evidence follow-up, November 22, 2026 — Reviewed; unresolved.** The source presents the 25-percent oil-and-gas and 9-percent coal shares as observations circulating in Chinese writing. The USGS's own assessment instead specifies undiscovered resources and gives separate gas and oil shares; it is not a table of all world reserves or a coal inventory. The route-saving claim also needs named endpoints and comparable routes. These three denominators cannot be repaired by inserting a later resource estimate or a different sailing-distance example. The same resource-definition check serves CMS08-R11.

**Remaining gap or scope limit.** Original Chinese resource and coal sources with their denominators; a reproducible route comparison for the distance-saving range.

**Earlier audit record (preserved).** Quoted claims, not verified (`unk`): the route-shortening figure comes from an epigraph and is not derived or sourced to a navigational calculation; the 25 percent and 9 percent resource shares are the Chinese authors' 'standard observation' and differ in wording (total oil and gas versus undiscovered hydrocarbons) from the USGS estimate the study cites elsewhere, so they should be read as Chinese talking points rather than established figures. Follow-up review, November 15, 2026. Separate the route comparison from the resource shares. A sailing-distance claim requires named origin and destination points and routes. The USGS resource estimates have a stated appraisal area and concern undiscovered conventional oil and gas. They do not reconcile the chapter’s broader denominators.
evidence: USGS assessment abstract, separate undiscovered oil and gas quantities

rows.usage: Illustrates the range of Chinese scholarly thinking on how to influence Arctic governance.
rows.finding: Accurately reported (`ok`): the three-option framework is quoted from Li Zhenfu's articles and the author notes Li rejects the first option as beyond China's current capacity; these are one scholar's views from a transport college and are not official policy, and the Chinese-language articles could not be re-retrieved.

rows.source: Legal Scholarship: Svalbard Treaty (1920) and UNCLOS Seen as 'Insufficient,' Antarctic Treaty Model, Dong Yue's Doubts, Extended Continental Shelf Rules (Scholarly Writing, pp. 15–30)
rows.usage: Shows that Chinese jurists examine the Arctic through UNCLOS, the 1920 Svalbard Treaty and the Antarctic model.
rows.finding: Consistent with the treaties' text (`ok`): the Svalbard Treaty affirms Norwegian sovereignty while granting equal access rights to signatories (China acceded in 1925), and the Antarctic Treaty freezes claims; the study correctly reports Chinese authors' view that these frameworks are inadequate, without testing the authors' legal reasoning.

rows.source: State Relations and Capabilities: Norway's Foreign Minister's August 2010 Praise, Iceland's President on 2008 Aid, Polar Research Institute (124 Staff; Three Antarctic and One Arctic Station), Xuelong (21,000 Tons) at 88°N and the North Pole (August 2010), Planned 8,000-Ton $300 Million Icebreaker by 2013 (pp. 33–46)
rows.usage: Documents China's practical investments and diplomatic overtures as of 2010.
rows.finding: Consistent with press reporting of the period (`ok · slip`): the Xuelong's August 2010 helicopter flight to the pole and the Norwegian and Icelandic statements are documented in the cited Russia Today, Barents Observer and Beijing Review articles; the planned $300 million 8,000-ton sister icebreaker due in 2013 was not built as stated (Xuelong 2, a larger ship, entered service in 2019), and the Polar Research Institute figure (124 staff) is a 2010 count.

rows.source: Overall Assessment: China Is 'Bound and Determined to Have a Voice, Perhaps Even a Say-So' in Arctic Affairs Despite Being a Non-Arctic State; Policy Not Yet Formulated (Introduction and Conclusion)
rows.usage: Provides the study's interpretive conclusion on China's Arctic intentions.
rows.finding:
**Open-claim evidence follow-up, November 22, 2026 — Reviewed; unresolved.** The bound-and-determined phrase is present on the supplied PDF p. 10 and is clearly the author's interpretation of public discussion and diplomatic conduct. A prediction about future influence is not itself an observed policy decision. Later observer status or a later white paper can be compared as subsequent events, but cannot authenticate an earlier undisclosed intention or prove a causal reading of diplomatic language. Keep the interpretation attributed and distinguish the contemporary evidence from hindsight.

**Remaining gap or scope limit.** A defined test and dated primary statements for the inferred intention; no new evidence establishes the hidden-motive interpretation.

**Earlier audit record (preserved).** Interpretive (`unk`): the judgment that Chinese diplomatic language about respecting Arctic states' sovereignty masks a determination to have a 'say-so' is the author's reading of articles and press rather than of government statements; later events (the 2013 observer status, the 2018 white paper) corroborate the direction but also show the policy was articulated more fully than the study allowed.

rows.source: Polar icebreaker replacement costs: per ship versus fleet cost
rows.usage: The note is attached to: “Until Congress and the White House come up with a plan to round up about $1.5 billion to keep the Polar Sea and Polar Star running, and another $1 billion or so to build replacements, the United States is an Arctic nation without that capacity.”
rows.finding:
**Open-claim evidence follow-up, November 22, 2026 — Reviewed; unresolved.** The historical CRS material distinguishes restoration, service-life extension and replacement. Its per-ship replacement estimates cannot establish the chapter’s juxtaposed fleet-wide US$1.5 billion upkeep and US$1 billion replacement totals without vessel count and price-year definitions. The GAO page was blocked during this check. The original press quotation and its cost scope remain separate from a verified procurement budget.

**Remaining gap or scope limit.** The original costed fleet/service-life plan and the exact quoted editorial’s vessel counts and price basis.

**Earlier audit record (preserved).** The 2010 CRS review reproduces a Coast Guard estimate of $800–925 million in 2008 dollars for one new polar icebreaker. Two ships at that estimate imply $1.6–1.85 billion before any adjustment. The passage does not say how many ships its roughly $1 billion buys. The cited amounts also require separate support for operating or extending the old ships’ service lives. Consistency review, November 14, 2026. CRS treats a new icebreaker's cost and extending existing vessels' service life as separate decisions. The 2008-dollar estimate supports a per-ship interpretation. CMS08-R10 discusses projected comparative fleet capacity and cannot validate either dollar total. Follow-up review, November 14, 2026. The contemporaneous CRS comparison gives a 2008-dollar estimate for one new heavy ship. Service-life costs for the existing ships and the number of replacement vessels are separate budget quantities. The referenced newspaper passage does not itself settle the scope of either estimate. Follow-up review, November 15, 2026. CRS gives a contemporary unit-cost range below $1 billion for a single new ship. The passage gives an aggregate replacement figure and does not identify the number of vessels or price basis. The two quoted budgets require a matching fleet and service-life plan. Source recheck. The 2010 GAO report explicitly states that the Coast Guard’s $800–925 million replacement estimate was per ship and in 2008 dollars. That documents the unit and price basis missing from the juxtaposed press estimates. The source of the $1.5 billion upkeep total and the replacement vessel count remain unresolved.

rows.source: Attribution of the population-proportional Arctic resource claim
rows.usage: The note is attached to: “A Chinese admiral said in early 2010 that since China has 20 percent of the world’s population, it should have 20 percent of the Arctic’s resources.”
rows.finding:
**Open-claim evidence follow-up, November 22, 2026 — Reviewed; unresolved.** Read the original March 6, 2010 Ta Kung Pao newspaper page A13. Its China News Service account attributes to Yin Zhuo the statement that China has one fifth of world population and cannot be absent from Arctic development. It does not state a numerical entitlement to one fifth of Arctic resources. SIPRI quotes the participation version; Brookings gives a stronger one-fifth-of-interests quotation from a different reporting trail. These are not interchangeable wordings. The newspaper page is valuable contemporary evidence, but cannot settle the paper's stronger resource-share attribution without the full interview or an independently authenticated transcript.

**Remaining gap or scope limit.** The original interview or recording establishing the precise one-fifth resource-entitlement wording.

**Earlier audit record (preserved).** Subsequent analyses repeat the one-fifth or 20% formulation attributed to Yin Zhuo, while other accounts quote a broader argument for Chinese participation. Repetition does not establish his original words. The original interview or speech and the cited Cnews report were not recovered. Treat the numerical entitlement formulation as an unverified attribution. Follow-up review, November 14, 2026. The newspaper is the source for a reported quotation, not the actual speaker’s transcript. Keep the claim attributed to the press unless the admiral, event and original language can be identified. The separate Arctic resource estimates in CMS08-R11 answer a different question. Follow-up review, November 15, 2026. Treat the numeric entitlement and the general argument for participating in Arctic issues separately. The later paraphrases do not show whether Yin Zhuo spoke of an entitlement, a demographic comparison or both. The named original interview remains unavailable. Source recheck. Contemporaneous Chinese-language and English-language reports attribute a demographic argument for participation to Yin Zhuo. The one-fifth figure in those reports describes world population. They do not substantiate the separate claim that he asserted a right to one fifth of Arctic resources. The archived full interview or its recording is still needed for that stronger attribution.

The paper reproduces a forecast, not an observed later fleet comparison. The supported verdict is confined to the quotation and its source trail; the eventual accuracy of the forecast remains unevaluated without fixed comparison dates and measures.

**Remaining gap or scope limit.** No remaining gap for the quoted forecast's presence in the NYT page; outcome testing and the underlying World Politics Review edition are separate questions.

**Earlier audit record (preserved).** The New York Times blog URL is identifiable, but its May 24, 2010 text was blocked from retrieval. The sentence is explicitly a forecast about two ships, not a claim that both were already operating in 2010. Later delivery dates alone do not disprove that a forecast was published. Neither the quotation’s exact wording and attribution nor the comparative criteria for larger and more modern were verified in this pass. Consistency review, November 14, 2026. Compare CMS08-R08's cost discussion with this prospective fleet comparison. The former's cost source cannot prove the words published by the newspaper. A direct copy of the May 24 article and a definition of vessel size are still needed. Follow-up review, November 14, 2026. The original passage attributes the statement to a May 2010 forecast. Later observations of fleet delivery measure the outcome and do not verify its quoted wording. The surviving article URL is enough to identify the missing archive item. Follow-up review, November 15, 2026. The study quotes a prospective comparison. The original blog text is needed to check the attribution. To assess the prediction itself, the intended ships and comparison date would have to be fixed, and the measures for size and modernity specified.

New York Times Ideas, China's Arctic Ambitions, May 24, 2010; quotation and explicit World Politics Review attribution

rows.source: Arctic resources: undiscovered recoverable petroleum versus all reserves
rows.usage: Note 37 reports a claim that the Arctic holds 25 percent of the world’s oil and gas, plus 9 percent of coal.
rows.finding:
**Open-claim evidence follow-up, November 22, 2026 — Reviewed; unresolved.** The USGS assessment abstract separately identifies about 30 percent of undiscovered gas and 13 percent of undiscovered oil north of the Arctic Circle. The EIA reproduction also identifies a conversion convention when aggregating petroleum quantities. Those are not all-reserve shares and contain no corresponding worldwide-coal inventory. The older Chinese 25-percent and 9-percent formulation still requires its own source and denominator. This is the same resource-definition comparison used in CMS08-R02, not an independent new discovery.

**Remaining gap or scope limit.** Original Chinese resource and coal sources, their appraisal dates and geographic/commodity denominators.

**Earlier audit record (preserved).** USGS’s 2008 appraisal concerns undiscovered conventional resources north of the Arctic Circle, not all known oil and gas reserves. Its estimates and the EIA summary use that narrower denominator. The cited Chinese authors’ exact 25 percent and coal figures were not retrieved. Specify the resource definition and assessment year, and distinguish reporting an author’s estimate from endorsing it as a geological fact. Rechecked November 14, 2026. The USGS publication quantifies the separate estimates at 13% of globally undiscovered oil and 30% of globally undiscovered gas. These percentages have different global denominators, and the study did not assess coal. The reported Chinese estimate remains open pending its original source and denominator. Follow-up review, November 14, 2026. The USGS assessment compares oil, gas and natural gas liquids separately and does not cover coal. CMS08-R09 instead concerns a press-attributed political remark. Keep the narrower USGS measure and the earlier Chinese figures under different attributions pending the Chinese original. Follow-up review, November 15, 2026. USGS treats undiscovered oil and gas as two different quantities and expresses their shares separately. A combined share needs a common energy-equivalent unit. The quoted coal estimate also requires a separate coal inventory and the original Chinese text.
evidence: EIA 2009 analysis of the appraisal, archived copy
USGS appraisal results in Science, 2009, abstract and assessment scope
EIA 2009 Arctic assessment, reproduced table and conversion convention

rows.finding: Reviewed November 15, 2026. CRS and a Coast Guard factsheet give 23 February 1978. The Coast Guard’s cutter page gives 1977, and its contemporary progress report says the vessel was delivered and placed in commission in January 1977. The original commissioning and status records are needed to reconcile the two dates. Follow-up review, November 15, 2026. The Coast Guard’s later institutional history and district factsheet support 1978, while its cutter profile and the contemporaneous account give 1977. Cite the precise milestone stated by each. The records reviewed do not yet establish whether the early status was distinct from the later commissioning. Source recheck. A contemporary Coast Guard progress-report collection preserves an institutional record from the period. The Coast Guard district fact sheet identifies February 23, 1978 as the commissioning date, while the previously linked cutter history gives 1977. Use the date with its source attribution until a dated commissioning program or unit log resolves the conflict. Source recheck. A contemporary account in October 1978 describes two ceremonies with different statuses. paper_memo.memo_title: Analytical & Source-Audit Memo: CMS-8 — The Dragon Eyes the Top of the World: Arctic Policy Debate and Discussion in China (David Curtis Wright, August 2011)

sections.heading: 1. Strategic Context & Core Thesis
sections.body: China Maritime Study No. 8 reads Chinese academic and popular writing on the Arctic from 2009–2010 to show how China thinks about a region where it is not a coastal state. Wright finds an unformulated policy but a consistent theme: the Arctic's routes and resources belong to all humankind, which sits awkwardly with China's insistence on state sovereignty and amounts to a quiet claim for a voice. Chinese authors see melting ice more as an economic opportunity than an environmental crisis, debate Canada's claims to the Northwest Passage, and call for stronger polar research and icebreaker capacity.

sections.heading: 2. Section-by-Section Analytical Breakdown
sections.body:
• **Introduction (pp. 1–9)**: Chinese interest, the 'all humankind' consensus and the sovereignty quandary.
• **Chinese Scholarly Writing (pp. 9–33)**: Ocean University of China series, game-theory and SWOT analyses, Li Zhenfu, legal scholars.
• **Arctic Environmental Issues and Canada's Claims (pp. 17–24)**: Environmental and sovereignty debates.
• **The Arctic in China's Popular Media (pp. 35–42)**: Nationalism, opportunity and naval calls.
• **Relations and Capabilities (pp. 33–46)**: Norway, Iceland, Russia, research stations, icebreakers.

sections.heading: 3. Key Doctrinal Concepts, Terminology & Quantitative Claims
sections.body:
• **Concepts**: *common heritage of all humankind*, *right to speak up* (话语权), *insert hands* (插手), *near-Arctic state* (a later phrase), *Northwest Passage as internal waters or international strait*, *Svalbard Treaty*, *SWOT*.
• **Quantitative claims**: route shortening `5,200–7,000 nm`; Arctic holds `25%` of oil and gas and `9%` of coal (Chinese 'standard observation'); admiral's `20%` population / `20%` resources; Polar Research Institute `124` staff, `3` Antarctic and `1` Arctic station; Xuelong `21,000` t, `88°N` (August 2010); planned icebreaker `8,000` t, `$300 million`, by `2013`.

sections.heading: 4. Audit Assessment & Analytical Significance
sections.body:
Of the 6 reference rows audited in `CMS-08`, 4 are rated `ok` (one with a slip) and 2 are rated `unk`; no `fix` was found:
• **`[CMS08-R02]` (`unk` — Resource and Route Claims)**: The figures are quoted talking points and differ in wording from the USGS estimate the study cites.
• **`[CMS08-R06]` (`unk` — 'Say-So' Conclusion)**: An interpretation overtaken by later formal policy.

The study is the **first English-language survey of Chinese Arctic discourse** and anticipates the 2013 observer status and 2018 Arctic white paper; it links to the polar research fleet in `CMR-03` (Snow Dragon) and to the energy-route and SLOC material in `CES-P1`. Its limits are its focus on 2009–2010 writings and the absence of official Chinese policy documents, which did not yet exist.

**Footnote rows**: all 133 footnotes were extracted and consolidated into 59 source rows in the Reference Audit Matrix (CMS08-N001 to CMS08-N131). Repeat citations of the same source within this paper, including Ibid. and short-form notes, share one row, which lists each note's passage and result. Footnote-level result: 133 notes: 23 (17%) are confirmed, 1 of them against a retrieved source and 22 after an outside web search (16 of the latter with a slip or an unchecked detail noted); 5 are flagged for reader check; 110 (83%) are not confirmed. Of the 110 notes not confirmed, 72 are Chinese-language sources that have not been searched in Chinese (a search in Chinese could settle some of them); 3 were judged not web-checkable (1 private interview or conversation; 1 note that is explanatory text or a fragment, not a citation; 1 other item); 35 were searched on the web without finding corroboration. A source row is `ok` only when every note in it is confirmed, and `fix` when a note is confirmed wrong; the paper's 59 source rows are 13 `ok`, 0 `fix` and 46 `unk`. Notes flagged for reader check, for example (the outside search found something a reader should look at; none is a finding that the author is wrong): `CMS08-N004`: The sentence quotes 25 percent of the world's undiscovered hydrocarbons as lying in the Arctic and attributes it to the USGS. The USGS 2008 Circum-Arctic Resource Appraisal gives about 13 percent of undiscovered oil, 30 percent of undiscovered gas and roughly 22 percent of undiscovered technically recoverable petroleum; the 25…; `CMS08-N022`: The sentence says a Chinese admiral said in early 2010 that since China has 20 percent of the world's population it should have 20 percent of the Arctic's resources (Cnews, 30 July 2010); `CMS08-N037`: The sentence says the Arctic potentially contains 25 percent of the world's oil and natural gas, 9 percent of its coal, and large amounts of diamonds and other minerals; and 2 more. 24 notes carry a reader note on how the note is displayed or cited.

sections.heading: Open claim-audit follow-up, November 22, 2026 (review complete; gaps recorded)
sections.body:
This continuation targets 12 initially open claim audits in this paper. 12 have a recorded individual follow-up: 1 now have a supported or correction finding; 11 remain unresolved. 0 of this paper’s initial open audits still await this continuation. Every reviewed row retains its evidence limits; a completed follow-up does not mean every substantive claim is verified.

rows.source: Framing: Post-2009 Deterioration (Cheonan, Japan–China Trawler Collision and Rare-Earth Restrictions, South China Sea Confrontations), Friedberg's Deterrence Argument versus Swaine's Cooperation Argument, 'Large Tent' of NTS Concerns (Introduction, pp. 1–4)
rows.usage: Sets up the volume's premise that nontraditional security is a more promising field for cooperation than deterrence.
rows.finding: Consistent with the public record and cited works (`ok`): the March 2010 Cheonan sinking, the September 2010 trawler collision near the Senkakus and the associated rare-earth export restrictions, and the Friedberg and Swaine quotations are accurately attributed; that NTS cooperation 'could build the trust necessary' for harder problems is Swaine's argument, not a demonstrated outcome.

rows.source: Gulf of Aden Mission and Hospital Ship: Seven Deployments and Eighteen Ships to December 2010, More Than 3,100 Ships Protected, Peace Ark's 88-Day 2010 Mission (Chapter 2, Gill, New Directions in Chinese Security Policy)
rows.usage: Quantifies the PLAN's first sustained far-seas NTS mission and its use as capability building.
rows.finding: Consistent with the cited source (`ok`): the figures are attributed to China's March 2011 defense white paper and match the escort tally Chinese authorities reported at the time; the December 2008 deployment date is correct, and the Peace Ark's 2010 deployment was the navy's first hospital-ship tour of Africa and South Asia.

rows.source: UN Peacekeeping: China Ranked 14th with 2,137 Personnel in Ten Missions (28 February 2010); France 16th (1,673), Russia 42nd (362), United Kingdom 46th (275), United States 71st (86 in Seven Missions); Largest of the P5 (Chapter 8, Blasko)
rows.usage: Shows China's growing role in peacekeeping relative to other great powers.
rows.finding: Internally consistent and consistent with UN data of the period (`ok`): the rank ordering (14th, 16th, 42nd, 46th, 71st) matches the personnel numbers listed, and China's lead among the five permanent members was correct in early 2010; the statistics are a single-date snapshot that has since changed substantially.

rows.source: Beijing Olympics Security: PLA 46,000 Troops, 98 Fixed-Wing Aircraft, 60 Helicopters, 63 Ships; PAP 85,000 Troops; Civilian Police Held Primary Responsibility (Chapter 8, Blasko)
rows.usage: Demonstrates the PLA's domestic NTS role and scale.
rows.finding: Consistent with the quoted official statement (`ok`): the numbers are given as a direct quotation of a Chinese statement ('46,000 troops, 98 fixed-wing aircraft, 60 helicopters, 63 ships…'), which the authors cite to Chinese media; the figures could not be independently verified, and the text notes that civilian police nonetheless led site security.

rows.source: Chinese Lessons from Mumbai (Sun Kai and Guo Peiqing): Seaborne Attack Begun 26 November 2008 from Karachi via a Pakistani Cargo Vessel and Hijacked Indian Fishing Boat; 'Resulted in 195 Deaths and More Than Three Hundred Wounded' (Chapter 7, pp. 77–86, Chapter 7)
rows.usage: Uses the 2008 Mumbai attacks as the case for Chinese analysis of maritime terrorism risks.
rows.finding: Needs correction on the casualty figure (`fix`): the official Indian toll was 166 victims killed (175 including the nine gunmen) and about 300 wounded, so the 195 figure is an early press estimate; the operational narrative (terrorists sailing from Karachi, hijacking an Indian fishing boat and killing its crew, three days to end the siege, Operation Black Tornado) is otherwise consistent with the public record.

rows.source: Complementarity Thesis and Cooperation Proposals: Pan Zhenqiang on NTS Cooperation, Gunness on China's 'Maritime Reemergence' (18,000 km Coastline, 1,400 Harbors, ~1,800 Merchant Ships, Six of the World's Top Ten Ports), Blasko on Peacekeeping Approaches (Chapters 8–10)
rows.usage: Draws the volume's conclusion that NTS cooperation is feasible and complementary.
rows.finding:
**Open-claim evidence follow-up, November 22, 2026 — Reviewed; unresolved.** The original chapter's PDF p. 128 supplies the coastline, harbor, merchant-ship and port-ranking figures, but those are separate populations with different units and dates. The national area is stated in square miles in that passage and should not be silently compared with a Chinese source expressed in square kilometres. The older audit's categorical claim that cooperation failed is also too broad: deterioration in relations cannot by itself measure the absence or effectiveness of all nontraditional-security cooperation. The statistical inputs and the causal expectation require separate tests.

**Remaining gap or scope limit.** The original dated transport/port statistics, the claimed maritime-area unit, and a defined causal test for the cooperation thesis.

**Earlier audit record (preserved).** Forward-looking and only partly borne out (`unk`): the Gunness statistics (an 18,000 km coastline, over 1,400 harbors, six of the top ten ports, about 1,800 ships) are cited to Chinese and maritime sources and were roughly accurate for 2010–2011 though the ship count understates later growth (compare the larger 2024 fleet counted in `CMR-51`); the volume's central expectation that NTS cooperation would ease naval tensions was not realized as relations deteriorated after 2012.

rows.source: Share of China’s foreign trade carried by sea: volume versus value
rows.usage: The note is attached to: “About 85 percent of China’s international trade uses shipping lanes.”
rows.finding:
**Open-claim evidence follow-up, November 22, 2026 — Reviewed; unresolved.** The contemporary Commerce Ministry services-trade account says more than 90% of foreign-trade goods travel by sea, without specifying a trade-value denominator. APEC’s national-fleet carriage percentages answer a different ownership/flag question. Neither authenticates the particular 85% in the cited Ocean Development Report. The chapter’s broad shipping dependence can be credible while the specific historical fraction remains unverified.

**Remaining gap or scope limit.** The cited report’s year, definition and underlying volume or value table.

**Earlier audit record (preserved).** China’s Commerce Ministry reported in 2024 that maritime transport carried 95% of foreign-trade freight volume. The statement separately reports trade value in currency. The later freight-volume figure cannot verify an undated 85% share of international trade in the earlier paper. The original Ocean Development Report table is needed to establish the year and unit behind 85%. Consistency review, November 14, 2026. APEC's shipping study distinguishes shares carried on national fleets from shares carried by sea. The older CMS13-R14 and CMS10-R02 estimates use their own dates and denominators. The 2010 Ocean Development Report page is needed to know what the 85% measures. Follow-up review, November 14, 2026. APEC Table 2-3 concerns the carriage share of national fleets. CN21C8-R07 also addresses that distinct denominator. Neither supplies the original Ocean Development Report value for all shipping lanes. The 85% needs a vintage and volume-or-value definition. The official report does not supply that alternative ranking basis. Preserve the Wenchuan figures as official reporting while withdrawing an unsupported all-deployments superlative.

**Remaining gap or scope limit.** The headcount counterexample is documented; a narrower peak-strength or duration-based ranking would still require a consistently defined historical series.

**Earlier audit record (preserved).** Reviewed November 11, 2026. The official totals match Chapter X, PDF page 25. The retrieved passage does not establish the largest-since-1979 comparison. That superlative needs a defined personnel measure and comparative deployment records, including other disaster responses. The totals are confirmed as official reporting, not independently enumerated headcounts. Consistency review, November 14, 2026. The official 2008 totals cover two named personnel groupings. The independent imagery audit CMS11-R07 measures a different aspect of response. No comparative personnel series corroborates the historical superlative. Cite the numbers as official reporting and leave the ranking open. Follow-up review, November 14, 2026. The 2008 white paper gives separate numbers for two groups. The cited totals do not supply a comparison against other deployments since 1979. Keep the total attributed to the white paper and identify the largest-since claim as needing a consistent comparison.

paper_memo.memo_title: Analytical & Source-Audit Memo: CMS-9 — Not Congruent but Quite Complementary: U.S. and Chinese Approaches to Nontraditional Security (Lyle J. Goldstein, ed., July 2012)

sections.heading: 1. Strategic Context & Core Thesis
sections.body: China Maritime Study No. 9 collects ten chapters by Chinese and American scholars on nontraditional security (NTS) — piracy, terrorism, peacekeeping, disaster relief — to argue that U.S. and Chinese approaches are 'not congruent but quite complementary.' Goldstein presents the volume as an alternative to a deterrence-only reading of U.S.-China maritime rivalry after the incident-ridden year 2009–2010: both sides name similar threats, China's NTS capacity (Gulf of Aden escorts, a hospital ship, peacekeeping, Olympic security) has grown rapidly, and the 'large tent' of NTS offers a practical basis for naval cooperation.

sections.heading: 2. Section-by-Section Analytical Breakdown
sections.body:
• **Introduction (Goldstein)**: The post-2009 deterioration and the NTS case.
• **Chapters 1–3 (Yu and Xiao; Gill; You Ji)**: NTS in the relationship; new directions in Chinese security policy; the Gulf of Aden mission.
• **Chapter 4 (Scobell and Stevenson)**: The PLA's rediscovery of NTS; Beijing Olympics.
• **Chapters 5–6 (Pang Zhongying; Goldstein and Walsh)**: Chinese peacekeeping; East Timor case study.
• **Chapter 7 (Sun and Guo)**: Chinese analysis of the Mumbai attacks and maritime terrorism.
• **Chapters 8–10 (Blasko; Pan Zhenqiang; Gunness)**: U.S. and Chinese peacekeeping; cooperation prospects; maritime reemergence.
• **Afghanistan and civilian peacekeeping**: The July 2010 Kabul address records the expanded zero-tariff exchange and the planned scholarship increase. The Langfang case documents the institutional development of civilian police training for peacekeeping.

sections.heading: 3. Key Doctrinal Concepts, Terminology & Quantitative Claims
sections.body:
• **Concepts**: *nontraditional security (NTS)*, *large tent*, *military operations other than war*, *peacekeeping and stability operations*, *maritime terrorism*, *capacity building*, *naval cooperation*.
• **Quantitative claims**: Gulf of Aden `7` deployments, `18` ships, `3,100+` ships escorted (December 2010); Peace Ark `88` days; peacekeeping `2,137` personnel in `10` missions (China `14th`; France `1,673`; Russia `362`; UK `275`; US `86`); Olympic security PLA `46,000` troops / `98` aircraft / `60` helicopters / `63` ships, PAP `85,000`; Mumbai `195` deaths (official `166`); coastline `18,000 km`, `1,400+` harbors, `~1,800` merchant ships.

sections.heading: 4. Audit Assessment & Analytical Significance
sections.body:
The initial claim audits flagged a casualty figure and the volume’s forecast for cooperation:
• **`[CMS09-R05]` (`fix` — Mumbai Death Toll)**: The chapter's 195 deaths overstates the official toll of 166.
• **`[CMS09-R06]` (`unk` — Cooperation Thesis)**: The forecast of easing tensions through NTS cooperation was not realized.

The volume is a **valuable record of the NTS cooperation agenda at its high-water mark** and an early source on Chinese peacekeeping, Gulf of Aden escort and hospital-ship diplomacy; it sets the background for `CMS-10` (a detailed study of the Gulf of Aden mission), `CMR-08` (naval diplomacy) and `CMS-06` (maritime confidence building). Its limits are its 2010–2012 data and optimistic reading of the cooperation prospects.

**Afghanistan and Langfang rechecks**: China’s foreign minister dated the expanded zero-tariff exchange of letters to March 2010 in his July 2010 Kabul address. The exchange covered more than 4,000 items and implementation still awaited domestic review. The signed tariff annex remains unavailable (CMS09-R61). The same address announced that annual scholarships would rise from 30 to 50 starting in 2011. An award register is needed to establish how many places were awarded that year (CMS09-R60). A peace-capacities study hosted by the UN corroborates the establishment of the Langfang civilian-police training centre in August 2000 (CMS09-R51).

**Footnote rows**: all 251 footnotes were extracted and consolidated into 210 source rows in the Reference Audit Matrix (CMS09-S1N001 to CMS09-S13N015). Repeat citations of the same source within this paper, including Ibid. and short-form notes, share one row, which lists each note's passage and result. Footnote-level result: 251 notes: 68 (27%) are confirmed, 0 of them against a retrieved source and 68 after an outside web search (45 of the latter with a slip or an unchecked detail noted); 5 are flagged for reader check; 183 (73%) are not confirmed. Of the 183 notes not confirmed, 79 are Chinese-language sources that have not been searched in Chinese (a search in Chinese could settle some of them); 15 were judged not web-checkable (3 notes that are fragments or run-on text attached to a Chinese-language source; 1 the authors' own data, imagery or analysis; 3 private interviews or conversations; 1 print-only book or paywalled item; 4 notes that are explanatory text or a fragment, not a citation; 3 other items); 88 were searched on the web without finding corroboration; 1 has not been searched. A source row is `ok` only when every note in it is confirmed, and `fix` when a note is confirmed wrong; the paper's 210 source rows are 51 `ok`, 0 `fix` and 159 `unk`. Notes flagged for reader check, for example (the outside search found something a reader should look at; none is a finding that the author is wrong): `CMS09-S4N008`: The sentence says Liu Huaqing's 1987 blue-water maritime strategy aimed to make the PLAN a powerful regional navy. Sources support 1987 for the endorsement of "near-seas active defense," but others date the CMC's "offshore defense" component to 1985 and Liu's three-stage naval plan to 1982, and describe the strategy in terms of…; `CMS09-S6N013`: The sentence says China's Ministry of Defense recently replied that China has no plan for overseas military bases. The copy of the cited China Daily report that could be retrieved (an ANI version) attributes the statement to a retired navy rear admiral who is an NPC deputy, and does not mention the ministry; a separate January…; `CMS09-S13N002`: The sentence says about 85 percent of China's international trade uses shipping lanes, citing the SOA Ocean Development Strategy Research Group's China's Ocean Development Report; and 2 more. 29 notes carry a reader note on how the note is displayed or cited.

sections.heading: Open claim-audit follow-up, November 22, 2026 (review complete; gaps recorded)
sections.body:
This continuation targets 14 initially open claim audits in this paper. 14 have a recorded individual follow-up: 1 now have a supported or correction finding; 13 remain unresolved. 0 of this paper’s initial open audits still await this continuation. Every reviewed row retains its evidence limits; a completed follow-up does not mean every substantive claim is verified.

[CMS09-R14](#audit?type=claim&paper=CMS-09&row=CMS09-R14): Correction established. The headcount counterexample is documented; a narrower peak-strength or duration-based ranking would still require a consistently defined historical series.

[CMS09-R06](#audit?type=claim&paper=CMS-09&row=CMS09-R06): Reviewed; unresolved. The original dated transport/port statistics, the claimed maritime-area unit, and a defined causal test for the cooperation thesis.

[CMS09-R07](#audit?type=claim&paper=CMS-09&row=CMS09-R07): Reviewed; unresolved. The cited report’s year, definition and underlying volume or value table.

[CMS09-R10](#audit?type=claim&paper=CMS-09&row=CMS09-R10): Reviewed; unresolved. The BBC original or Financial Times interview for exact wording and translation, particularly the first quotation.

[CMS09-R20](#audit?type=claim&paper=CMS-09&row=CMS09-R20): Reviewed; unresolved. The original press conference and a dated SHADE rotation/authority record.

[CMS09-R35](#audit?type=claim&paper=CMS-09&row=CMS09-R35): Reviewed; unresolved. The original UN statement and clear separation of the Indonesian proposal, ASEAN agreement and later training-centre implementation.

[CMS09-R37](#audit?type=claim&paper=CMS-09&row=CMS09-R37): Reviewed; unresolved. The 2007 Beijing regional annual-report passage or a dated event record specifying audience and predeployment timing.

[CMS09-R50](#audit?type=claim&paper=CMS-09&row=CMS09-R50): Reviewed; unresolved. Annual agendas or diplomatic records identifying dates, event identity and hosts for the claimed series.

[CMS09-R52](#audit?type=claim&paper=CMS-09&row=CMS09-R52): Reviewed; unresolved. The original comparative study or contemporaneous facility inventory and ranking method.

[CMS09-R53](#audit?type=claim&paper=CMS-09&row=CMS09-R53): Reviewed; unresolved. Separately dated cumulative and current series with personnel categories, repeat-deployment rules and mission coverage.

[CMS09-R60](#audit?type=claim&paper=CMS-09&row=CMS09-R60): Reviewed; unresolved. A 2011 country-specific award/placement table or implementation notice, distinct from offered places.

[CMS09-R65](#audit?type=claim&paper=CMS-09&row=CMS09-R65): Reviewed; unresolved. The negotiating record or independent participant evidence for the specific mediation claim, distinct from the authorization vote.

[CMS09-R69](#audit?type=claim&paper=CMS-09&row=CMS09-R69): Reviewed; unresolved. The final presenter/attendance record, with planned invitees separated from actual participation.

[CMS09-R70](#audit?type=claim&paper=CMS-09&row=CMS09-R70): Reviewed; unresolved. The complete set of cited speeches and an explicit distinction between illustrative sequence and ranked policy priority.

rows.source: Why Antipiracy: Apolitical Threat, Economic Costs, Need for International Cooperation, Domestic and External Pressure for Leadership, a 'Low-Risk Opportunity' to Test Beijing's Preferences (Introduction, pp. 15–20)
rows.usage: Explains why Beijing chose antipiracy as its first regularized overseas naval deployment.
rows.finding: Consistent with the cited Chinese and Western sources (`ok`): the legal definition of piracy quoted (UNCLOS Article 101) is accurately paraphrased and the argument that piracy is 'private' and thus politically convenient is supported by the Chinese commentary cited; the analysis of motivations is the authors' synthesis rather than a Chinese statement of intent.

rows.source: Chinese Dependence on Shipping: MoT's Ju Chengzhi (2009): Over 3,300 Vessels, 84.88 Million Tonnes, Fourth in the World, 90 Percent of International Trade by Sea, '40,000 Crewmen'; Port Throughput Projected from 1.8 to 3 Billion Tons by 2010 (Chapter 1, pp. 30–35)
rows.usage: Quantifies China's maritime commercial vulnerability as a driver of the Gulf of Aden mission.
rows.finding:
**Open-claim evidence follow-up, November 22, 2026 — Correction established.** A direct English–Chinese comparison resolves the seafarer discrepancy. The English passage on the supplied PDF p. 26 quotes Ju Chengzhi as saying 40,000 crewmen. Note 58 on PDF p. 47 prints the Chinese original as 40万名船员: 400,000, not 40,000. This is a tenfold translation/transcription error within the report's own quoted material; it need not be explained by comparison with a much later two-million registered-mariners total. Correct the English rendering to 400,000 while retaining its historical and source-attributed scope. The separately bundled fleet size, carrying-capacity and ranking figures still need their original contemporaneous statistical definitions and are not independently certified by this internal correction.

**Remaining gap or scope limit.** The crew translation error is established; the other historical fleet measures and their original statistical denominator remain separately unverified.

**Earlier audit record (preserved).** Quoted figures, not reconciled (`unk`): the statistics are a Chinese ministry official's 2009 claims; the '40,000 crewmen' figure is inconsistent in scale with the roughly two million registered mariners documented later (`CMR-51`), which suggests it counts only a subset (for example, ocean-going officers on Chinese-flag ships) and the study does not say which; the 3,300-vessel, 84.88 million-tonne and fourth-place figures could not be matched to a published ranking in this pass.
evidence: No Substitute for Experience, correct publisher record; PDF pp. 26 and 47, quoted Chinese text in note 58

claim_review.original_source: Chinese Dependence on Shipping: MoT's Ju Chengzhi (2009): Over 3,300 Vessels, 84.88 Million Tonnes, Fourth in the World, 90 Percent of International Trade by Sea, '40,000 Crewmen'; Port Throughput Projected from 1.8 to 3 Billion Tons by 2010 (Chapter 1, pp. 30–35)
claim_review.original_usage: Quantifies China's maritime commercial vulnerability as a driver of the Gulf of Aden mission.
claim_review.remaining_gap: The crew translation error is established; the other historical fleet measures and their original statistical denominator remain separately unverified.

rows.source: 2008 Piracy Impact on Chinese Shipping: 83 of 1,265 Chinese Ships Attacked (January–November 2008), Tianyu Seizure (Repaired by PLAN Mechanics in Six Days), Zhenhua 4 Attack (17 December), 86 Percent of Netizens Supporting a Mission, Over 17,000 in the People's Daily Survey (Chapter 1, pp. 36–40)
rows.usage: Shows the immediate threat and public pressure preceding the first deployment.
rows.finding: Consistent with press records (`ok`): 83 of 1,265 is 6.6 percent, the Zhenhua 4 attack on 17 December 2008 and the Tianyu seizure are reported by Chinese and international media, and the survey figures are given with media citations (Notes 110–111); the survey results are online polls and not representative samples.

rows.source: First Deployments and Operations: Wuhan, Haikou and Weishanhu Leave Sanya (26 December 2008); First 14 Task Forces' Port Calls (Feb 2009–Apr 2013); 26 December 2012 Three-Fleet Display; Djibouti, Salalah and Aden Resupply (Authors' Note; Chapters 4–5)
rows.usage: Documents the scale and logistics pattern of the escort force.
rows.finding: Consistent with public records (`ok`): the first task force's departure from Sanya on 26 December 2008 with Wuhan, Haikou and Weishanhu matches PLAN announcements, and the use of Djibouti and Salalah for replenishment is widely documented; the port-call table was legible only in part, so individual dates and ports could not be fully checked.

rows.source: Rescues of Chinese Ships by Others: Iranian Navy Frees 28 Sailors of Xianghuamen (Seized ~45 Miles off Jask, April 2012); May 2011 Chinese-Flagged Cargo Ship Pirated, 24 Crew in Safe Room Freed by Indian and NATO Forces (Chapter 1, pp. 40–41)
rows.usage: Shows the PLAN is not the only force protecting Chinese shipping.
rows.finding: Consistent with the public record (`ok`): the April 2012 seizure of the Xianghuamen and its rescue by Iranian forces and the May 2011 incident involving an Indian-NATO rescue of a Chinese-flagged ship are reported by international media, and the text correctly notes the owner (Nanjing Ocean Shipping Company).

rows.source: Conclusion: 'No Substitute for Experience,' PLAN-MoT Coordination, a 'Coming-of-Age' for the PLAN Within a Ground-Force-Dominated PLA, Possible Influence on Maintenance Procedures and Ship Design (Conclusion, pp. 199–201)
rows.usage: Summarizes the authors' judgment of the mission's institutional and operational effects.
rows.finding:
**Open-claim evidence follow-up, November 22, 2026 — Reviewed; unresolved.** On PDF p. 199 the authors expressly say autonomy should not be exaggerated and identify improved coordination as a condition for realizing the potential they describe. Coming-of-age is an analytical characterization, not an independently measured organizational status. Evidence of an escort deployment or some coordination does not establish how much autonomous authority the navy gained or how later ship design changed because of the mission. Preserve the authors' caveats and the distinction between observed activity and inferred institutional effect.

**Remaining gap or scope limit.** Dated authority, coordination and design-decision records sufficient to attribute the claimed institutional changes to the missions.

**Earlier audit record (preserved).** Interpretive and partly supported (`unk`): the Chinese sources cited document improvements in logistics and training, but statements that the mission will influence ship design, make the PLAN assume 'unprecedented responsibility' in civil-military coordination and let it 'emerge from under the PLA's shadow' are the authors' inference; they themselves caution that the PLAN's autonomy 'should not be exaggerated.'

claim_review.original_source: Conclusion: 'No Substitute for Experience,' PLAN-MoT Coordination, a 'Coming-of-Age' for the PLAN Within a Ground-Force-Dominated PLA, Possible Influence on Maintenance Procedures and Ship Design (Conclusion, pp. 199–201)
claim_review.original_usage: Summarizes the authors' judgment of the mission's institutional and operational effects.
claim_review.remaining_gap: Dated authority, coordination and design-decision records sufficient to attribute the claimed institutional changes to the missions.

rows.source: Appendix: Notional PLAN Order of Battle by Fleet (SSBNs, Attack Submarines, Carrier, Destroyers, Frigates, Amphibious Ships, Patrol Craft, Mine Warfare and Auxiliary Ships; 2012 Estimates with Bracketed Alternates) (p. 202)
rows.usage: Offers a snapshot of PLAN force structure at the time of the study.
rows.finding:
**Open-claim evidence follow-up, November 22, 2026 — Correction established.** The original extraction problem was overcome by rendering and reading the entire appendix table on PDF p. 202. Parentheses are Military Balance 2012 alternatives; brackets are the separately compiled Erickson/Jane's estimates. They must not be summed as additional vessels. A concrete classification/date error appears in note d: it says two Type 052D destroyers were commissioned in January 2013 and cites Changchun. Contemporary reporting identifies Changchun, commissioned January 31, 2013, as Type 052C; the first Type 052D, Kunming, entered service in March 2014. Thus note d requires correction, not merely improved extraction. The table remains a source-dependent historical estimate with separate alternatives; this verdict does not independently certify every fleet subtotal or class inventory.

**Remaining gap or scope limit.** The note-d error is established. Complete independent reconciliation of every 2012/2013 alternative fleet count still requires the separately dated source inventories.

**Earlier audit record (preserved).** Not checkable from the extracted text (`unk`): the table's columns and bracketed alternate estimates are interleaved, with footnote letters embedded, so the fleet-by-fleet numbers could not be read or compared with other published orders of battle; the figures are 2012 estimates and would in any case be superseded.
evidence: Contemporary commissioning report, February 1, 2013, Changchun identified as Type 052C
Xinhua, December 11, 2015, Changchun's class and January 31, 2013 commissioning
Xinhua, February 17, 2015, distinction between Changchun and the first Type 052D's March 20, 2014 commissioning

claim_review.original_source: Appendix: Notional PLAN Order of Battle by Fleet (SSBNs, Attack Submarines, Carrier, Destroyers, Frigates, Amphibious Ships, Patrol Craft, Mine Warfare and Auxiliary Ships; 2012 Estimates with Bracketed Alternates) (p. 202)
claim_review.original_usage: Offers a snapshot of PLAN force structure at the time of the study.
claim_review.remaining_gap: The note-d error is established. Complete independent reconciliation of every 2012/2013 alternative fleet count still requires the separately dated source inventories.

rows.source: Which Chinese energy plan set the 2015 natural-gas share target?
rows.usage: The note is attached to: “China’s eleventh five-year guideline (2006–10) reiterated the goal of the tenth five-year plan (2001–2005); it addresses environmental concerns and diversification of energy supply by, first, increasing natural-gas consumption to 8 percent of total energy use by 2015 and, second, finding new sources of oil to reduce China’s reliance on coal.”
rows.finding: The 12th Five-Year energy plan documents gas production, transmission and LNG reception targets for 2015. Those indicators are distinct from natural gas’s share of total energy use. The exact 8% target and its attribution to the 11th guideline were not established in the plan text checked. The target needs a dated policy source that explicitly defines the denominator. Consistency review, November 14, 2026. Note 47 is a May 2012 report explicitly about the Twelfth Plan submission. That timing cannot document wording of the earlier Eleventh guideline. Compare CESP1-R13, which gives 2020 for the same 8% figure. Preserve different target years until a plan or official annex establishes the provenance. The official Twelfth Plan text can be checked separately from the actual 5.9% share reported for 2015 by NBS. Follow-up review, November 14, 2026. The official Twelfth Five-Year energy plan gives a dated planning comparator. The linked citation is a May 2012 report about that plan’s submission. It cannot establish that the Eleventh guideline reiterated a Tenth-plan 8% target. Keep the target’s provenance open even though the NBS actual series can be identified. Follow-up review, November 15, 2026. The energy plan issued in January 2013 and the natural gas plan notice issued in December 2012 belong to the Twelfth Five-Year Plan. They cannot date the 8% target to the Eleventh plan. The earlier guideline passage and the contemporaneous definition of total consumption are the outstanding evidence. Source recheck. The published Eleventh Five-Year Energy Development Plan and China’s second UN climate communication give the plan’s gas target as 5.3% of primary energy consumption by 2010. The cited May 2012 source concerns the Twelfth Plan, not the Eleventh. The claim that the Eleventh reiterated an 8% target for 2015 should be corrected or supported with a different instrument.
evidence: NEA notice for the Twelfth Five-Year natural gas plan
China’s second national communication, energy policy section

rows.source: China’s advocacy for a piracy court inside Somalia
rows.usage: The note is attached to: “Beijing has repeatedly attempted to solve this complex issue by advocating the establishment of such a court on Somali soil.”
rows.finding:
**Open-claim evidence follow-up, November 22, 2026 — Reviewed; unresolved.** China’s January 2011 UN statement supports improving prosecution and judicial capacity. The report’s stronger proposition combines a specific venue inside Somalia with repeated advocacy. A reference to Somali jurisdiction or international agreement does not locate the courtroom, and one statement cannot establish repetition. The UN catalogue returned a non-document response in this continuation.

**Remaining gap or scope limit.** A readable venue-specific statement and a second dated occurrence, or the original cited Xinhua record.

**Earlier audit record (preserved).** The UN Secretary-General’s 2011 report examines modalities for specialized Somali anti-piracy courts, including the relationship between venue and Somali jurisdiction. A UN proposal does not establish that China repeatedly advocated a court physically on Somali soil. That narrower attribution remains unverified pending multiple dated Chinese statements that specify location. Consistency review, November 14, 2026. Separate Chinese support for prosecution and Somali capacity from the precise proposal on venue. The May 2011 Chinese statement is a further dated source. The original linked June article and a second express statement about courts physically in Somalia remain necessary to establish repetition. Follow-up review, November 14, 2026. China’s UN mission statement supports strengthening prosecution and judicial capacity. For the narrower geographic assertion the original Xinhua report and another dated statement explicitly placing the court on Somali soil are still needed. Support for Somali jurisdiction alone does not settle venue.
evidence: China's UN mission, May 2011 Security Council piracy statement

claim_review.original_source: China’s advocacy for a piracy court inside Somalia
claim_review.original_usage: The note is attached to: “Beijing has repeatedly attempted to solve this complex issue by advocating the establishment of such a court on Somali soil.”
claim_review.remaining_gap: A readable venue-specific statement and a second dated occurrence, or the original cited Xinhua record.
previous_evidence: China's UN mission, May 2011 Security Council piracy statement

rows.source: Month of Peace Ark’s first Seychelles visit
rows.usage: The paper dates the hospital ship’s first Seychelles visit to November 2010.
rows.finding: The Seychelles presidency’s retrospective explicitly places the first visit in October 2010. Use October for the arrival or first visit. The retrospective does not independently establish a departure date or the April 2011 visits mentioned in the same sentence.

rows.source: China’s March 2011 reserves and the reported Treasury share
rows.usage: The note is attached to: “China officially held over three trillion dollars in foreign reserves in March 2011, almost half of which was in the form of American Treasury bonds.”
rows.finding: Contemporaneous reserves were reported at about $3.04 trillion. The historical monthly Treasury series as reproduced for March gives about $1.145 trillion for mainland China, about 38% of the reserve figure. The Treasury benchmark survey gives a different date and coverage. Country-attributed Treasury holdings include more than the reserve manager’s own portfolio and may be attributed through custodians. The published figures do not substantiate the claimed portfolio share of almost half. Consistency review, November 14, 2026. The cited April Caixin article concerns investment of reserves, while the Treasury comparison rests on a country-attributed March holdings figure. Approximately $1.145 trillion divided by $3.04 trillion is 37.7%. Present that as a comparison of published series, with ownership and custody limitations.
evidence: U.S. Treasury 2011 foreign portfolio holdings benchmark

rows.source: China’s Somalia peacekeeping assistance: total versus per recipient
rows.usage: The note is attached to: “For example, as of late 2011 China had given the African Union (AU) $2.2 million to use specifically for peacekeeping in Somalia and also $780,000 to the governments of Burundi and Uganda for supplies to be used in the African Union Mission in Somalia (AMISOM).”
rows.finding: Wang Min’s November 2011 statement confirms US$2.2 million in cash for AU peacekeeping operations in Somalia. It separately reports RMB 5 million each to Uganda and Burundi for logistical supplies. At roughly RMB 6.4 per U.S. dollar, that is about $780,000 each, or about $1.56 million combined. The paper should specify the amount per recipient and identify the dollar figures as conversions.

rows.source: Claimed evacuation from Fiji during the 2006 coup
rows.usage: The note is attached to: “Subsequently, China has organized a variety of NEOs, including from Fiji during the 2006 military coup.”
rows.finding:
**Open-claim evidence follow-up, November 22, 2026 — Reviewed; unresolved.** The November 2006 foreign-ministry statement expressly describes evacuating people from Tonga through Fiji. That is a different origin and crisis from an evacuation from Fiji during its coup. The report’s private 2009 conversation cannot be independently reconstructed from this consular notice. Transit via Fiji should not be used as verification of the claimed Fiji evacuation.

**Remaining gap or scope limit.** A Fiji-specific contemporary evacuation record, passenger accounting or the original interview documentation.

**Earlier audit record (preserved).** A contemporaneous Chinese government notice confirms a chartered evacuation from Tonga in November 2006. Tonga is a separate case and does not corroborate an evacuation from Fiji. The chapter’s source is a private 2009 meeting, and a public Fiji evacuation record was not located. Retain the distinction and leave the Fiji claim unverified. Consistency review, November 14, 2026. The private 2009 discussion is the cited basis for the Fiji assertion. No public Fiji operational record was confirmed. Apply the event-specific standard in CMR04-R08 and leave the documented 2006 Tonga evacuation attributed to Tonga. Follow-up review, November 14, 2026. The consular announcement expressly identifies Tonga, even though it relates to the same year and part of the Pacific. It cannot verify Fiji. The private 2009 discussion, or a contemporaneous Fiji-specific passenger or consular record, remains necessary.
evidence: Chinese government notice on the Tonga charter, November 2006

claim_review.original_source: Claimed evacuation from Fiji during the 2006 coup
claim_review.original_usage: The note is attached to: “Subsequently, China has organized a variety of NEOs, including from Fiji during the 2006 military coup.”
claim_review.remaining_gap: A Fiji-specific contemporary evacuation record, passenger accounting or the original interview documentation.
previous_evidence: Chinese government notice on the Tonga charter, November 2006

rows.source: The reported 86% Eastday online poll
rows.usage: The note is attached to: “The media outlet Eastday reported that a survey showed that 86 percent of Chinese “netizens” (active Internet users) supported a Gulf of Aden mission.”
rows.finding: A contemporary Sina item reports the same 86% result. That supports the reported online poll figure, while the underlying questionnaire and sampling method were not recovered. The figure describes respondents to an online poll and does not establish a representative share of all Chinese internet users.

rows.source: Foreign-flag shares in the escort statistics
rows.usage: The source row and CMS10-S7N086 contain nearly equal Chinese/foreign shares in one passage and roughly 70% foreign in another.
rows.finding:
**Open-claim evidence follow-up, November 22, 2026 — Reviewed; unresolved.** The introductory escort summary describes roughly equal Chinese and foreign shares, whereas another cited passage uses about 70% foreign. The study contains multiple historical cutoffs and measures escort operations, protected vessels and task forces separately. The original later ministry link encountered a certificate failure. No matched-date numerator/denominator pair was recovered, so this is a reconciliation gap rather than a demonstrated percentage error.

**Remaining gap or scope limit.** The dated underlying escort tables for both passages, with repeat transits, flag/nationality and cutoff definitions.

**Earlier audit record (preserved).** These are different approximate shares. The citing passages alone do not establish that they cover identical dates or the same universe of escort operations. Reconcile each numerator, denominator and cutoff date before treating this as an arithmetic error. The later official ten-year total is a different observation window.

claim_review.original_source: Foreign-flag shares in the escort statistics
claim_review.original_usage: The source row and CMS10-S7N086 contain nearly equal Chinese/foreign shares in one passage and roughly 70% foreign in another.
claim_review.remaining_gap: The dated underlying escort tables for both passages, with repeat transits, flag/nationality and cutoff definitions.

rows.source: Chinese merchant traffic and pirate attacks in the first eleven months of 2008
rows.usage: Notes 105 and 106 support 1,265 Chinese merchant transits, of which 83 were reportedly attacked.
rows.finding:
**Open-claim evidence follow-up, November 22, 2026 — Reviewed; unresolved.** The December 18, 2008 Foreign Ministry briefing directly gives 1,265 Chinese commercial-ship transits in the first eleven months, says 20 percent were attacked, and separately describes seven hijacking cases involving China. The chapter's 83 is not reproduced by that briefing: 83/1,265 is about 6.56 percent, whereas 20 percent implies about 253. An additional 2010 legal article's indexed passage attributes 83 disturbed vessels to the Chinese Shipowners' Association, suggesting a different reporting stream and possibly a different incident category. That indexed lead is not a substitute for the association's original tally. Keep the shipowner count, ministry percentage and hijacking cases separate.

**Remaining gap or scope limit.** The original Shipowners' Association tally and incident definitions reconciling 83 disturbed/attacked vessels with the ministry's separate percentage.

**Earlier audit record (preserved).** The 18 December 2008 Foreign Ministry briefing gives the same 1,265 transits but says 20% were attacked, which implies roughly 253. It also separately counts seven hijacking cases involving China. The briefing therefore does not substantiate 83. The cited magazine and newspaper accounts need matching definitions of attempted attacks, attacked vessels and hijackings before the figures can be reconciled. Consistency review, November 14, 2026. Read the December 18 briefing as the source of 1,265 trips, a 20% figure and seven hijacking cases. Do not use those categories as interchangeable counts. As in CMS05-R09 and CMS10-R17, cite the incident definition and scope before comparing the 83 figure.
evidence: Foreign Ministry briefing, December 18, 2008, commercial transits, attack percentage and hijacking cases
2010 International Journal of Marine Affairs and Fisheries article, lead to the separately attributed association tally

claim_review.original_source: Chinese merchant traffic and pirate attacks in the first eleven months of 2008
claim_review.original_usage: Notes 105 and 106 support 1,265 Chinese merchant transits, of which 83 were reportedly attacked.
claim_review.remaining_gap: The original Shipowners' Association tally and incident definitions reconciling 83 disturbed/attacked vessels with the ministry's separate percentage.

rows.source: Threefold piracy increase: timeframe and metric
rows.usage: The note is attached to: “According to a report by Zhongxing News Network citing European Union (EU) naval officials, the number of pirate attacks rose threefold in 2010.”
rows.finding:
**Open-claim evidence follow-up, November 22, 2026 — Reviewed; unresolved.** The source is a July report and cannot represent a completed calendar-year 2010 observation. NATO’s later annual incident series uses an explicitly defined ship population, which may differ from attacks counted by the original EU briefing. Without its cutoff, area and baseline, a threefold rise cannot be tested against full-year global totals.

**Remaining gap or scope limit.** The original July Chinese dispatch and EU briefing, including period, area and incident definition.

**Earlier audit record (preserved).** The cited People’s Navy item appeared July 2, 2010, so its reference to this year cannot by itself establish a completed full-year comparison. NATO’s later standardized series lists 117 attacks in 2009 and 127 in 2010, while treating disruptions and approaches separately. That does not support an unqualified threefold annual rise, but may use a different geography, reporting period or measure. Retrieve the underlying Zhongxing/EU account and specify its baseline before deciding the precise correction. Consistency review, November 14, 2026. Apply the same geographic and incident definitions required by CMS05-R09 and CMS10-R16. NATO's final calendar-year figures cannot rule out an increase over a shorter interval in the July Chinese report. The original account's reporting window and baseline remain unidentified. Follow-up review, November 14, 2026. The source date and the words this year establish that the July article could not have been using complete calendar 2010 figures. To confirm a threefold rise, identify the cutoff, geography and incident definition. The annual comparator alone cannot resolve those fields.
evidence: NATO 2013 annual report, piracy series and definitions

claim_review.original_source: Threefold piracy increase: timeframe and metric
claim_review.original_usage: The note is attached to: “According to a report by Zhongxing News Network citing European Union (EU) naval officials, the number of pirate attacks rose threefold in 2010.”
claim_review.remaining_gap: The original July Chinese dispatch and EU briefing, including period, area and incident definition.
